notes: WebSearch could not be used for this part: its first call was answered that the session's search allowance was already spent. Pages were reached directly, with the kit's honest User-Agent and each site's robots.txt read first: the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (read from the scratch copy of the database that had run the files step), each government's own site, the two state parties' sites and local party units' sites, the Minnesota Historical Election Archive by a candidate's own address, KAXE's and Eden Prairie Local News's own site search, and pages those link to. No search engine was read in place of the search tool. Candidates with nothing below are the ones this left out of reach.

Not read, because the site refused scripts or asks them to stay out: mncourts.gov (403, robots.txt included: no court page for either judge, and nothing at all for Adam Johnson); Wabasha County's site (robots.txt: nothing for Jason Bade); the City of Hugo's site (robots.txt: nothing for Mark Koll); the Senate District 33 Republicans' site (403); vote4edina.com, the website David Frenkel filed, whose robots.txt tells Claude's readers by name to stay out, so the site was not read and no website finding is recorded for him (the filed address stands on its own); and newspapers whose robots.txt names Claude's readers (hometownsource.com, presspubs.com, southernminn.com, mankatofreepress.com, republicaneagle.com, messagemedia.co, postbulletin.com) or closes its search pages to scripts (inforum.com, brainerddispatch.com, duluthnewstribune.com, pineknotnews.com). Belle Plaine Public Schools' site did not answer (connection refused); Tri-City United's board page and the Clay County DFL's candidates page draw their names by script and gave none.

Tim Dummer: the state DFL's list of endorsed candidates links, beside his name, an address on Google Sites (sites.google.com/view/timdummerformn) that today shows a page about a card-game app in Hindi and nothing about him. It is not recorded. The website recorded for him was found through the Chisago-Isanti DFL's page and read. John may want the state party's link left out wherever a page copies it.

Birth years from the Minnesota Historical Election Archive: for Tim Dummer, Ron Case and Brendan VanAlstyne the archive's page gives a full date and names a state birth certificate index among its sources (parts 6 and 9 met the same thing). Only the year is recorded, each with a note; whether a year with that trail is shown is John's decision. Dan Kessler's page cites only the Chaska Herald.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): the Carver County Republican Party names "Tim Litfin for Mayor" beside the City of Waconia's logo under "City Council and Mayors: Recommended Candidates", and keeps the word "Endorsed" for statewide and legislative candidates. It is kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls it an endorsement. The same page says of the other candidate in Chrissy Ahola's race only that he "represents County Commissioner District 2".

Read and left out on purpose: ages given as "age on Election Day" (KAXE's guides, for Monique Doward and Sarah Speer), which do not fix a birth year; jobs, schools, family and faith, wherever a page gave them; boards that are not government posts (an electric cooperative, a lake association, nonprofit boards); Sean Thomas's fire department post and his seat on a district input team; Chrissy Ahola's own description of her views on her home page, which names no party; Tom Murphy's line "I am a township supervisor for Maine Township" on a campaign page dated 2022 (he is a sitting legislator and the Legislative Reference Library lists no other government service for him); county party units' pages that list Lisa Demuth among their candidates (Carver, Olmsted, Goodhue, Clay), since the state party's own release is cited; and the Forward Party's Minnesota page, which shows only a feed of sign-ups and no endorsement. Home addresses and other contact details printed on some official pages were not recorded anywhere.

Monique Doward: our list carries her party as "FI" with a note that the full name is not in the Secretary's files. KAXE's guide gives "Party: Forward Independence", and her answer there speaks of herself "as a Forward Independence candidate". No party page publishing an endorsement of her was found.

For the second reader: (1) Shelley Buck and Tom Murphy are sitting legislators with roster records; for Buck two posts the Legislative Reference Library lists under other government service are given (not her House seat; one is an elected office in a tribal government, which her own campaign site also leads with, and whether a card shows it is John's decision), and the Library gives no birth date for her ("uncertain"); for Murphy only the website. No party page naming Murphy's 2026 endorsement was found (the Otter Tail County Republicans' site has no candidates page). (2) Lisa Demuth's leadership posts take their years from the session the Library files them under. Her own_words quote is cut from a longer sentence on her About page so as to leave out the part that speaks of race. (3) Ron Case's and Timothy Litfin's mayoral start years are left blank because no page prints them (see each "also"). (4) Kip Bruender has a page of his own on the county's site, which also prints a home address; the Board of Commissioners page carries the same facts without it and is the one cited. Austin Public Schools' Board Members page prints members' contact details beside their titles; it is the only district page that states Peggy Young's office. (5) Charles D. Halverson's entry rests on a 2020 radio piece and has no dates. (6) Patrick Murphy: KAXE's guide has "District 1" in one line and District 3 everywhere else. (7) Brendan VanAlstyne's own site and the archive spell the family name "Van Alstyne"; the same person by Shakopee, the office and the campaign site filed for this race. (8) Karen MacLaughlin's site shows a script-drawn page, so the kit's fetch step may take nothing from it.

No findings: Scott Steffes (the county's page shows another commissioner holds the seat and is not on the list; the Clay County Republicans' candidates page lists no county race), Joshua Stehr (the Goodhue County Republicans' pages name no one for sheriff), Jason Bade, David Frenkel, Mark Koll, Rebecca Rand (the City of Owatonna's page shows another member holds the Fifth Ward seat), Christopher Potter, Brandon A Brockway and Adam Johnson. None of them has a page in the election archive, and no review item arose: nothing our record shows was contradicted by an official page.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address in this file was opened again with the kit's fetcher, each one answered, and each finding was read on its page. Also re-read: the two candidates' About pages, Eden Prairie Local News, KAXE's Brainerd guide and Orono's 2026 election page named under "also". The Carver County Republicans' page does place "Tim Litfin for Mayor" after the City of Waconia's logo under Recommended Candidates; it stays under party_support, not endorsed_by. The state DFL's list still links Tim Dummer to the Google Sites address; the Chisago-Isanti DFL links to timdummerformn.com. Karen MacLaughlin's site gives only its description line to a script. Contact details printed on several official and campaign pages were not recorded.
